subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Areas of study and set works

questions.q: Which musical element describes the loudness or quietness of the music?
questions.explain: Dynamics is the element that deals with how loud or quiet the music is.

questions.q: What does the Italian tempo marking 'Allegro' mean?
questions.explain: Allegro indicates a fast, lively tempo.

questions.q: The instruction 'pizzicato' tells a string player to do what?
questions.explain: Pizzicato means to pluck the strings with the fingers rather than using the bow.

questions.q: A single, unaccompanied melodic line is described as which texture?
questions.explain: Monophonic texture consists of a single melodic line with no accompaniment.

questions.q: What does the dynamic marking 'pp' stand for?
questions.explain: 'pp' stands for pianissimo, meaning very quiet.

questions.q: What does the dynamic marking 'forte' mean?
questions.explain: Forte (f) means loud.

questions.q: Which OCR Area of Study includes music such as samba, bhangra and calypso?
questions.explain: Rhythms of the World covers traditional music from around the globe, including samba, bhangra and calypso.

questions.q: In a concerto, what is a 'cadenza'?
options: A recurring theme for the full orchestra
A virtuosic solo passage, often unaccompanied
A short introduction before the main theme
questions.explain: A cadenza is a showy, virtuosic passage for the soloist, frequently unaccompanied and sometimes improvised.

questions.q: A perfect cadence, which gives a strong sense of ending, moves between which chords?
questions.explain: A perfect cadence moves from chord V to chord I, creating a finished, conclusive sound.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a polyphonic texture?
options: A melody supported by chordal accompaniment
Two or more independent melodic lines sounding together
All parts moving in the same rhythm
questions.explain: Polyphonic (contrapuntal) texture combines two or more independent melodic lines at the same time.

questions.q: In a Baroque concerto, what is the 'ritornello'?
options: A recurring theme played by the full ensemble
An improvised solo for the soloist
The final chord of the piece
questions.explain: The ritornello is the recurring theme played by the whole ensemble, returning between solo sections in Baroque concertos.

questions.q: In film music, a recurring musical theme linked to a particular character or idea is known as a?
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a recurring theme associated with a specific character, place or idea in film music.

questions.q: Film music that comes from a source the characters can hear on screen, such as a car radio, is described as?
questions.explain: Diegetic music originates within the world of the film and can be heard by the characters themselves.

questions.q: Which structure is most typical of songs studied in The Conventions of Pop?
questions.explain: Most pop songs are built on an alternating verse and chorus structure.

questions.q: Music written in a minor key is most often described as having what character?
questions.explain: Minor tonality typically creates a sad, dark or serious mood, in contrast to the brighter major key.

questions.q: Which description best fits a homophonic texture?
options: A single melody with no accompaniment
A main melody supported by chordal accompaniment
The same melody performed at different pitches at once
questions.explain: Homophonic texture has one clear melody supported by chords or accompaniment beneath it.

questions.q: A piece has a time signature of 3/4. How many beats are there in each bar and of what value?
questions.explain: In 3/4 the top number gives three beats per bar and the bottom number (4) shows each beat is a crotchet.

questions.q: A passage is marked 'Adagio, pp, legato'. How would it most likely sound?
options: Slow, very quiet and smoothly connected
questions.explain: Adagio means slow, pp means very quiet, and legato means the notes are played smoothly and connected.

questions.q: You hear music that is fast and lively, with short detached notes played loudly. Which set of terms describes it?
questions.explain: Allegro (fast/lively), staccato (short and detached) and forte (loud) together match this description.

questions.q: In Rhythms of the World you notice strong accents falling on the weaker, off-beat parts of the bar. What is this feature called?
questions.explain: Syncopation is the accenting of off-beats or normally weak beats, a common feature in much world music.
